sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: before you drive: tires, seat and mirrors, safety belts, air bags, child passengers, loads and driver assistance
Audience: every first-time South Carolina Class D applicant, with the child restraint stages also aimed at drivers who carry young children.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the primary safety belt enforcement law that lets an officer stop an unbelted driver is set out here [A06], and so are the car seat, booster and belt stages a driver must follow for child passengers [A07].
Level: mostly recall with a few exact values (seat distance, mirror viewing gain, child ages and height) plus practical setup procedures.
Prerequisites: none beyond the earlier sections; this section prepares the vehicle checks a learner uses again on the skills test.

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.
